card: This pull request raises the minimum C++ standard to C++23 across CMake, depends, and CI, raising minimum compiler versions to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It deletes in-tree polyfills like util::Expected and custom byteswap routines in favor of std::expected and std::byteswap, and adopts C++23 features like container contains, std::to_underlying, and optional transform across 65 files. The author states that workarounds to avoid C++23 are accumulating while subprojects already rely on C++23 constructs. The change is intended to unblock further modernization tracked in #34979.
changed_since_previous: Added commits adopting further C++23 features across the codebase: `std::ranges::contains`, `std::to_underlying`, range-based `string_view` constructors, and `std::optional::transform()`, along with include-what-you-use cleanups.
evidence: The author notes: "C++23 for Bitcoin Core is mostly a 'style update' on top of C++20. However, the workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating and some parts of the code already use C++23 features, such as lambda attributes (libmultiprocess@bdd0cd6)."
The PR description links to #34979 as modernizations unlocked by bumping compiler requirements.
problem: Maintaining compatibility with C++20 requires carrying internal polyfills and shims while barring newer standard library patterns. Meanwhile, code complexity increases as external dependencies and internal workarounds increasingly bump up against C++23 features.

risk.why: Bumping compiler version requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19 affects all downstream builders and toolchains, while widespread standard library replacements across multiple subsystems could introduce subtle functional regressions.

scope_notes: This is marked as an RFC/WIP draft. It combines build system standard bumps with mechanical across-tree replacements utilizing C++23 language and library features.
summary: This pull request raises the required C++ standard from C++20 to C++23 across CMake, depends, and CI environments, establishing minimum compiler requirements of GCC 13 and Clang 19. It drops internal polyfills including `util::Expected`, custom byteswap shims, and `ALWAYS_FALSE` in favor of standard library equivalents (`std::expected`, `std::byteswap`, and C++23 `static_assert(false)`). It also refactors call sites across the codebase to use C++23 facilities such as `container::contains()`, `std::ranges::contains()`, `std::to_underlying()`, range-based `std::string_view` construction, and `std::optional::transform()`.
